coachTips.title: Improve your writing speed
coachTips.text: Three habits that build real speed. One: when copying or making notes, do not write word-by-word with your eyes on the source - read the whole sentence, then write it from memory without looking back; this trains the mind-to-fingers link that speed comes from. Two: set a timer for 5, 10 or 15 minutes and write as fast as you can for just that window - short daily sprints make speed a habit. Three: read as many books as you can; words you have seen often live in your mind as pictures, and a word you can picture is a word your hand writes without hesitating.
coachTips.why: shown as a general practice habit for every writer
examples: read the whole line - look away - write it

coachTips.title: The 10 letters that improve your handwriting
coachTips.text: Ten letters - A, D, H, I, L, M, N, R, T, U - end on a downstroke. When a word ends with one of them (on this page: 'brown', 'over', 'a') finish it with a small upward stroke instead of stopping dead on the vertical. 'Hand' should not end abruptly on the 'd' stem - the small finishing flick is what makes the word look complete.
coachTips.why: shown because this page has 38 words ending in the ten finishing letters
examples: A D H I L M N R T U

coachTips.title: Five letters, one c: the rhythm secret
coachTips.text: Five letters - a, d, g, q and o - are all built on the same c. When each of them carries an identically shaped c, the word gains a rhythm the eye reads as beautiful; when the c inside d is fatter than the c inside a, the same word looks unsettled. Always start these letters with the c as their base: practise one honest c, then extend that exact c into a, into d, into g, into q, and close it into o. Keep the c the same size and shape across all five and the rhythm takes care of itself.
coachTips.why: shown because this page uses 5 of the five c-built letters (a d g q o)
examples: c -> a  d  g  q  o

coachTips.title: Just for fun: what an old graphologist would read in your letter n
coachTips.text: Old-school graphology claimed the letter n shows how you decide: sharp, pointed n's were read as a quick, decisive thinker; flat-topped or rounded n's as someone who gathers every fact before choosing. A fun mirror to hold up to your page - and only that: graphology is folklore, not science. None of your scores use it; the 20 factors measure the writing, never the writer. Enjoy it like a fortune cookie.
coachTips.why: your page has 22 letter n's - this card is for curiosity, not coaching
examples: n with sharp peaks - n with round tops
